transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-17
Time: 15:00 PST (45m)
Attendees: Alice Rivera (Redwood AE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (Redwood CSM); Priya Patel, Marcus Lee, Tomas Alvarez, Lena Ortiz (Skylark)

Summary:
Brief planning sync focused on go-live / rollout plan for the POC. Discussed canary approach, A/B routing, monitoring and alerting, runbooks, and a final load test. Security asked about KMS integration and audit logs. Agreed on next steps: share canary policy, run test, deliver pricing, and finalize cutover date.

Topics:
- Canary & A/B rollout strategy
- Monitoring, SLOs, and alerts
- Runbook and rollback playbook
- Performance/load testing and gate criteria
- Security interview: KMS / audit / SOC2
- Pricing / Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs

Transcript:
[00:00] Alice Rivera: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep this to about 45 minutes. quick agenda  canary plan, monitoring, runbooks, and the load test.
[00:18] Priya Patel: Sounds good. we're really targeting a 99.9 p99 latency for our user flows, okay if we shorthand that as p99 < 300ms for the main inference path?
[00:28] Daniel Cho: yeah, so from the POC numbers we've been hitting p95 around 120ms, p99 is kind of in the 260-320 range depending on sequence length and the KV cache hit rate. there's some variance when the cache misses and we see the cold KV cash load, sorry, KV cache load.
[00:45] Marcus Lee: and that's with the current batch settings?
[00:49] Daniel Cho: right now it's our test config: batch size 8, dynamic batching, and a small prefix cache enabled. for production we recommended a slightly higher batching policy but tuned to keep the p99 target so tradeoff cost vs latency.
[01:05] Priya Patel: ok makes sense. for go-live we want predictable cost too, so we were looking at Redwood Dedicated vs Hosted. what's the work to switch later if we start hosted and then move to dedicated?
[01:20] Alice Rivera: great q. the control plane and API are the same  routing policy and model pinning carried across. moving to dedicated is mostly infra provisioning and capacity reservation; we do the migration for you. timeline's typically 2-4 weeks depending on GPU availability.
[01:36] Tomas Alvarez: from security side, we need to confirm KMS integration and HSM support, also audit logs retention for 13 months. do you have those docs?
[01:46] Maya Singh: yes, we'll send the SOC2 and KMS/HSM integration guide after the call  link in the next steps. retention and export of audit logs is supported, and we'll include the exact retention SLAs.
[02:02] Lena Ortiz: on canary, what's your recommended ramp strategy? 5% then 25% then cutoff?
[02:08] Daniel Cho: typical we do a gradual canary: start 5% for 2 hours, then 25% for 4 hours, then 50% for -- pardon, 50% for a day before full cutover. but you can define guardrails: error rate > 0.5% or latency regressions p99 + 20% triggers rollback. we can also do A/B test with two model variants if you want to compare quantized vs full-fp.
[02:35] Marcus Lee: what about automatic fallback? if the dedicated pool is saturated can you fallback to hosted?
[02:41] Alice Rivera: yes, smart routing supports multi-tier fallback (region/capacity tier/model variant). we can set policy to prefer dedicated and then fallback to hosted compatible variant in same region  we should test that path in the load test.
[02:55] Priya Patel: load tests  we'd like to replicate weekday peak and weekend baseline. can you run the load test against our staging endpoint with masked PII?
[03:04] Daniel Cho: absolutely. we'll need your sample traffic (anonymized) and auth creds for the staging route. prefer a 2-hour sustained peak and a 30-minute spike. that should surface autoscale behaviour and KV cache cold starts.
[03:21] Priya Patel: I'll export sample logs, strip PII, and share via secure link. due by Thursday.
[03:28] Alice Rivera: perfect. we'll also provide a runbook template for cutover  steps, rollback, owners, post-cutover monitoring checks.
[03:36] Tomas Alvarez: on runbooks, include escalation contacts and the exact queries to pull audit logs, please. also want to see verified SSO/SAML integration flow.
[03:45] Maya Singh: noted  we'll include SSO diagrams and example SAML metadata exchange.
[03:51] Marcus Lee: quick question on observability  can Redwood emit traces to our Datadog and also provide token-level cost breakdowns?
[03:58] Daniel Cho: yes to both. we have tracing hooks and per-token cost reporting; we'll wire a Datadog forwarder and share dashboard templates.
[04:06] Lena Ortiz: what are our go/no-go gate criteria for cutover?
[04:09] Alice Rivera: proposed gates: successful load test with p99 within 20% of target, no security blockers from Tomas, runbook signed off, and capacity provisioning done for Dedicated if chosen.
[04:19] Priya Patel: timeline  we prefer go-live the week of Jan 10, 2027. that gives us time to run tests and doc reviews.
[04:26] Alice Rivera: sounds realistic. action items recap in a minute. any other questions?
[04:31] Marcus Lee: one last  pricing for burst capacity during cutover?
[04:34] Alice Rivera: we can offer burst credits for one week at a capped rate; I'll include scenarios in the pricing doc.
[04:40] Priya Patel: great, thanks everyone.
[04:43] Alice Rivera: recap next steps: we'll share canary policy draft, runbook template, SOC2/KMS docs, and schedule load test. redwood SE will run test on 12/22 if we get traffic before then.
[04:58] Daniel Cho: thanks, I'll follow up with the test plan and a spreadsheet for traffic profiles.
[05:04] Tomas Alvarez: thanks all.

End of recording.
